content:
The Observatory expects today's maximum outdoor temperature to reach 34 degrees, close to the 2022 record "hottest Great Heat" of 34.9 degrees, and about 4 degrees higher than last year's "Great Heat".

The Observatory has issued the Very Hot Weather Warning, forecasting generally fine weather today, but with showers in some areas from morning to noon, and very hot temperatures during the day. In addition, a subtropical high pressure ridge is bringing fine weather to Hong Kong, but the coast will also be affected by showers.

The heatwave caused by the "Great Heat" has made Hong Kong's streets as hot and stuffy as an oven, with a thermometer at Mong Kok MacPherson Playground recording a high temperature of 40.8 degrees.

In past Great Heat days, the highest maximum temperature was 34.9 degrees in 2022, and the lowest was 22.2 degrees in 1965.

In addition, the highest average relative humidity and highest total rainfall recorded on Great Heat in past years were 96% and 195.1 millimetres in 1994, while the lowest average relative humidity was 70% in 1968.
